description: S1 and S2 heart sounds recorded over the mitral valve area in a healthy adult Beagle; used as reference/baseline recording.
Companion video/digital phonocardiogram (DPCG) synced recording for the normal rhythm example.

diagnosis: Mild mitral insufficiency (myxomatous mitral valve disease)
description: Grade 2/6 holosystolic plateau murmur, early myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD).
Grade 3/6 holosystolic plateau murmur consistent with mild mitral insufficiency.
Grade 4/6 holosystolic plateau murmur, severe mitral insufficiency in a geriatric dog.
Grade 3/6 systolic crescendo-decrescendo murmur, congenital pulmonic stenosis in a juvenile dog.
Grade 5/6 crescendo-decrescendo murmur, severe congenital pulmonic stenosis.
Grade 4/6 systolic crescendo-decrescendo murmur, severe congenital subaortic stenosis.
Grade 5/6 continuous 'machinery' murmur, classic for PDA.
Grade 4/6 holosystolic plateau murmur, restrictive VSD in a puppy.
Very soft, localized murmur detected only in a quiet room after intently listening.
Soft murmur but easily heard after a few seconds of auscultation.
Moderate-intensity murmur, readily audible on auscultation.
Loud murmur, not accompanied by a palpable precordial thrill.
Very loud murmur accompanied by a palpable precordial thrill.
Loudest murmur grade; palpable thrill remains audible even with the stethoscope lifted off the chest wall.
Regular, accelerated heart rhythm together with a systolic grade 5/6 murmur from mitral insufficiency.
Regular rhythm, slower than physiologic heart rate.
Bradycardia with an isolated ventricular extrasystole (VES) audible at approx. 8 seconds.
Rhythm variation linked to the parasympathetic/vagal effect during expiration; a normal finding in dogs.
Isolated premature atrial extrasystole at ~1 second, with concurrent grade 4/6 mitral murmur.
Isolated premature ventricular extrasystoles at ~2nd, 6th and 15th seconds.
Two ventricular extrasystoles of different morphology at 7th-8th seconds, plus a premature atrial extrasystole at the 11th second.
Abnormal, chaotic rhythm with an associated grade 3/6 mitral murmur.
Atrial fibrillation with an additional premature ventricular complex at ~10 seconds.
Focal fast tachycardia originating from atrial muscle.
Premature ventricular extrasystole at ~8 seconds; possible additional ES at 3rd/9th seconds.

diagnosis: Ventricular extrasystole (audible but not visible on ECG)
description: Premature extrasystole at ~6 seconds audible on the digital phonocardiogram but not visible on simultaneous ECG; concurrent sinus arrhythmia and grade 5/6 murmur. Illustrates auscultation catching what ECG alone might miss.
A run of bizarre/wide ventricular complexes followed by a return to fast regular sinus beats.
Two runs of ventricular extrasystoles with differing morphology/frequency, interspersed with regular fast sinus beats.
Isolated P waves without a following QRS complex at ~1st, 2nd, 4th and 6th seconds.
Complete AV dissociation: atria and ventricles beat independently; atrial contractions visible at ~1st, 3rd and 6th seconds.

Auscultation at the aortic valve (left 4th intercostal space). Regular rhythm, clear S1-S2 (lub-dub), no murmurs or skipped beats. Recorded with an Eko Core digital stethoscope; slide 16 of the UQ learning resource.
Auscultation at the mitral valve (left 5th intercostal space). Regular rhythm, clear S1-S2, no murmurs or skipped beats. Recorded with an Eko Core digital stethoscope; slide 17.
Auscultation at the tricuspid valve (right 4th intercostal space). Regular rhythm, clear S1-S2; slight skin-twitch/background noise present. Recorded with an Eko Core digital stethoscope; slide 18.

diagnosis: Normal heart sounds (tricuspid valve, realistic field recording)
description: Realistic example of what is typically heard auscultating the tricuspid valve in the majority of horses (soft window behind the right elbow), with superimposed gastrointestinal (GIT) sounds. Illustrates a common normal-but-noisy real-world auscultation. Recorded with an Eko Core digital stethoscope; slide 19.

Regular rhythm with an extra third heart sound (S3) producing a 'gallop' rhythm; a gallop is rarely pathogenic in horses and can arise from split S1, split S2, S3 or S4. Recorded with an Eko Core digital stethoscope; slide 20.
Holosystolic/pansystolic murmur of greatest intensity at the mitral valve, regular rhythm, no skipped beats. Recorded with an Eko Core digital stethoscope; slide 29.

diagnosis: Mitral regurgitation (murmur radiation heard at aortic valve)
description: Same mitral regurgitation case auscultated over the aortic valve region: holosystolic/pansystolic murmur of lesser intensity than at the mitral valve, illustrating murmur radiation. Recorded with an Eko Core digital stethoscope; slide 30.

diagnosis: Ventricular septal defect (VSD), auscultated at mitral valve
description: Regular rhythm with an abnormal holosystolic/pansystolic murmur, no skipped beats; definitive diagnosis required echocardiography. VSD murmurs in horses are typically audible on both left and right sides of the chest. Recorded with an Eko Core digital stethoscope; slide 32.

diagnosis: Ventricular septal defect (VSD), auscultated at aortic valve
description: Same VSD case auscultated at the aortic valve: regular rhythm, abnormal holosystolic/pansystolic murmur; recording includes background movement/GIT sounds. Recorded with an Eko Core digital stethoscope; slide 33.

diagnosis: Pentalogy of Fallot (auscultated at mitral valve)
description: Case from a horse referred to in the source material as 'UQ Billy'; regular rhythm with an abnormal systolic murmur that can be accompanied by pulmonary regurgitation sounds. Pentalogy of Fallot (VSD + pulmonic stenosis + overriding aorta + right ventricular hypertrophy + an atrial septal defect) is described as very rare in horses; definitive diagnosis required echocardiography. Recorded with an Eko Core digital stethoscope; slide 37.

diagnosis: Pentalogy of Fallot (auscultated at aortic valve)
description: Same 'UQ Billy' pentalogy of Fallot case auscultated at the aortic valve: regular rhythm, abnormal systolic murmur. Recorded with an Eko Core digital stethoscope; slide 38.

diagnosis: Pentalogy of Fallot (auscultated at tricuspid valve)
description: Same 'UQ Billy' pentalogy of Fallot case auscultated at the tricuspid valve: systolic murmur, potentially accompanied by pulmonary regurgitation sounds. Recorded with an Eko Core digital stethoscope; slide 39.
Irregularly irregular rhythm, classic for atrial fibrillation, a common and clinically important equine arrhythmia. Recorded with an Eko Core digital stethoscope; slide 47.
Same atrial fibrillation case auscultated at the mitral valve; irregularly irregular rhythm. Recorded with an Eko Core digital stethoscope; slide 48.

diagnosis: 2nd degree AV block (auscultated at aortic valve)
description: Regularly irregular rhythm with dropped/missed beats (S1-S2 pairs absent on schedule), consistent with 2nd degree AV block — common as a physiologic finding in fit/resting horses with high vagal tone, but can also be pathologic. Recorded with an Eko Core digital stethoscope; slide 52.

diagnosis: 2nd degree AV block (auscultated at mitral valve)
description: Same 2nd degree AV block case auscultated at the mitral valve; regularly irregular rhythm with dropped beats. Recorded with an Eko Core digital stethoscope; slide 53.
